transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-05
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (StrataHealth EM), Liam O'Connor (StrataHealth Platform Lead), Sofia Ruiz (StrataHealth SRE)
Shared: sizing spreadsheet (drive link), last week's perf logs, PoC run notes

Summary (auto): weekly POC sync focused on Dedicated sizing and autoscale behaviour. Reviewed last week's benchmark (p95/p99 latency, throughput), discussed warm-pool and burst strategies, identified tests to run and owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everybody, thanks for joining, we are on for 45, so quick agenda review — perf results, autoscale policy discussion, burst planning, next steps. sound good?
[00:18] Maya: yep, sounds good, thanks.
[00:22] Priya: I'll open the sizing sheet and the latest perf logs, give a quick rundown of what we saw from last week's check-in.
[00:30] Priya: ok so, quick recap, the test was a steady-state fan-out of token generation using the 13B open model, batch size we used was 8, kv cache hit was about 78% across the workload, we saw p95 around 220ms and p99 spikes up to 480ms when the cluster scaled up.
[00:53] Liam: those p99 spikes are the concern for us; the user-facing latencies can't go above 300ms for chat flows, otherwise product folks will push back.
[01:05] Priya: totally. note that some of the spikes line up with cold starts on new nodes — the warm pool wasn't fully sized. we also noticed the autoscaler had a 90s cool-down which caused a bit of oscillation.
[01:20] Jordan: to be clear, on Dedicated we recommended a warm-pool of N-1 nodes for the initial phase and a pre-warm policy for expected scheduled bursts. did we try pre-warming in that run?
[01:31] Priya: no pre-warm in that run, it was reactive; we wanted to establish baseline first. next run we can enable pre-warm and set lower scaling step sizes.
[01:40] Sofia: quick q — when you say warm pool, do you mean full GPU nodes that are hot, or containers on existing nodes?
[01:47] Priya: full nodes with the model loaded and KV cache primed — that's what gave us the fastest ramp. containers-only warmers are quicker to instantiate but you still get some model load time.
[01:56] Maya: ok, budget-wise how expensive is keeping N-1 warm 24/7? that's part of our cost tradeoff we need to present to finance.
[02:05] Jordan: fair. the sizing sheet has scenarios: baseline (no warm pool), moderate warm (one node warm), aggressive warm (N-1). I'll push a cost delta column, but rough rule-of-thumb — warm pool adds fixed idle cost but saves on p99 SLA failures.
[02:22] Priya: another lever is KV cache persistence across restarts; if we can persist KV caches to local NVMe and remap quickly, cold penalty reduces. but that's a deeper infra change.
[02:35] Liam: can Redwood do KV cache persistence now or is that roadmap?
[02:38] Priya: right now we have approachs — we support cache warm-up via snapshots and faster model load paths through quantized checkpoints; fully persistent KV across reboots is planned but we can emulate persistence with a fast pre-warm job.
[02:51] Jordan: quick aside — there was a small transcriptation glitch last time where Redwood Dedicated was referred to as "Redwood dedicate" on the doc, ignore that.
[02:59] Maya: ha, noted.
[03:02] Priya: turning to autoscale policies: we recommend a two-tier policy — reactive target-based scaling on CPU/GPU utilization for typical traffic, plus schedule-based scaling for predictable windows (end of month loads, marketing bursts). for bursts larger than X we suggest temporary on-demand fallback to Hosted for overflow.
[03:23] Liam: fallback to Hosted is interesting — does that meet our data residency/compliance needs? some traffic can be processed offsite?
[03:31] Jordan: good question — for StrataHealth we proposed a region-restricted Hosted fallback within your allowed region. also we can route only non-sensitive requests to Hosted and keep PHI on Dedicated.
[03:44] Maya: we do have PHI in some prompts; routing rules need to be strict. also audit logs and KMS integration are must-haves.
[03:54] Priya: we have KMS/HSM integrations and can keep keys in your tenant. audit logs are available via the Console; we'll attach compliance docs in the follow-up.
[04:05] Sofia: about the burst capacity numbers — last week's run hit ~18k tokens/sec at peak. can we size Dedicated to handle 25k burst with an acceptable p95?
[04:15] Priya: for 25k tokens/sec, rough calc is N x g5.12x equivalents, with batching tuned. I'll add a scenario in the sheet — but key is prefix reuse; higher KV hit reduces compute.
[04:29] Jordan: also consider model quantization to reduce GPU memory and improve throughput, at small quality tradeoffs. Maya, are you open to quantized 4-bit runs for the PoC?
[04:40] Maya: possibly, but product wants to validate output quality. we can run side-by-side evals.
[04:45] Priya: we'll include a quality check (BLEU-ish + manual spot checks) in the next run.
[04:52] Jordan: ok next item — autoscaler cooldown and step sizes. current config used 90s cooldown and scale by 2 nodes; that led to oscillation. recommended: 30-45s cooldown with max step +1 node, and a conservative lower bound to prevent thrash.
[05:09] Liam: reduce step to +1 will increase time to ramp for big sudden spikes though. how do we prevent missing SLOs during the ramp?
[05:17] Priya: answer is multi-pronged: warm pool, smaller step size but lower cooldown, and transient burst handling via fallback hosted or reserved burst capacity. Redwood Dedicated supports reserved burst capacity for customers — it's a paid buffer of standby nodes for short bursts.
[05:32] Maya: what's typical cost of reserved burst, like 4 hours/day over month?
[05:36] Jordan: depends on config, we'll put a sample in the sheet. it's usually cheaper than permanently sizing for peak.
[05:43] Maya: ok.
[05:45] [07:10] Priya: I'm looking at the perf trace — around minute ~12 of the run we see a scheduler queue backlog as new nodes spun up, p99 increases. I think tuning the scheduler and scheduler batching windows will help. some of this is infra-level.
[07:27] Liam: is that something Redwood operations can tweak during PoC or do we need a joint on-call?
[07:34] Priya: we can tweak config for the PoC and run multiple iterations; major infra changes would be roadmap.
[07:40] Sofia: can we get a run with pre-warm + reserved burst + quantized model to see best-case latency numbers?
[07:49] Priya: yes that's on our list. I'll run three variants: baseline (no warm), pre-warm only, and pre-warm+reserved-burst+quantization.
[07:57] Jordan: timing — Priya, can you do the heavy run this week?
[08:02] Priya: I'll schedule it for Thu 2025-05-08 morning UTC to match Strata peak; will share perf logs.
[08:09] Maya: good. also please include the pod startup times and model load times in the logs.
[08:14] Priya: will do.
[08:16] Jordan: next, the team's asked about throttling and rate-limits — if we want to protect the Dedicated cluster, you can set per-route quotas and reject or queue requests; recommend graceful degradation with a fallback model or Hosted route.
[08:33] Liam: that could work. product expects soft-fail with a lighter model when Dedicated is saturated. what's Redwood's light-model offering?
[08:41] Jordan: we can route to a smaller open model instance or to Hosted ephemeral endpoints. we'll add a routing plan to the doc.
[08:49] Maya: security — confirm SSO/SAML and RBAC for RBAC controls we need for dev/stage/prod separation.
[08:58] Priya: we support SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC; we'll attach the admin guide.
[09:04] Jordan: ok, let's capture next steps — Priya runs tests, Jordan update sheet, Maya confirm compliance window. Any blockers?
[09:12] Maya: none immediate, but procurement might ask for SOC2 type 2 evidence — can you include that?
[09:18] Priya: yes, we'll send SOC2 and ISO docs after the call.
[09:22] Sofia: small note: in the last logs there were a couple of misattributed hostnames in the metric tags; might make correlating harder. if you can normalize tags that'd be great.
[09:33] Priya: noted, we'll normalize tags and include a mapping table.
[09:37] Jordan: cool. any other questions?
[09:40] Liam: one more — how does Dedicated handle model rollouts? we want canary + auto rollback if quality regresses.
[09:48] Priya: Redwood supports canary rollouts with traffic splits, A/B config, and automatic fallback on error or on quality regression if you feed eval metrics — we can wire your eval harness to trigger rollbacks.
[09:59] Maya: good.
[10:02] Jordan: ok quick recap of action items then close.
[10:06] Jordan: Priya will run: baseline, pre-warm, pre-warm+reserved-burst+quantized; collect p95/p99, kv hit, pod start, model load times — due 2025-05-09.
[10:20] Jordan: I will share updated Dedicated sizing sheet with cost deltas for warm pool and reserved burst — due 2025-05-07.
[10:30] Maya: I'll confirm compliance window and any dataset restrictions by 2025-05-12.
[10:36] Liam: I'll provide current prod peak qps and proxy lat windows - due 2025-05-08.
[10:42] Jordan: we'll follow up with SOC2/ISO docs and a short technical deep dive if the perf run needs it.
[10:47] Maya: thanks everyone, this was useful.
[10:50] Jordan: thanks, we'll reconvene next week same time unless you want to move.
[10:55] Priya: thanks all.

End of transcript.

Notes/Artifacts to attach: sizing spreadsheet link (updated), perf-logs-2025-05-01.zip (shared), SOC2-summary.pdf (to send).

Meeting ended: 15:45 UTC
